correctness.rationale: All 85 projective lines are the precisely labeled source lines of arXiv:2609.26862v1. Every coefficient is represented exactly in the 32-dimensional Q-basis of Q(i, fourthroot(2), fourthroot(3)), whose independence follows from Gaussian valuations and Kummer theory. All 3,570 pairwise determinants are evaluated symbolically. The resulting graph has the independently published 850 edges and 20-regular / 530-320 common-neighbor profile. A concrete 18-line independent set gives the lower bound. A 19-clique cover of all vertices forces a 19-skew set to avoid repeated covering vertices; among eight residual four-element blocks all 4^8=65,536 transversals contain an intersection. The stand-alone checker executed and an independent exact recursive search also rules out 19. Infinite claims beyond the one fixed surface are not made.

originality.rationale: The initiating primary paper specifies and exhausts all 85 lines, reports a Picard rank and contrasts a distinct 79-line surface with 24 skew lines; it does not give the maximum number skew on the named 85-line member. The closest published exact incidence-spectrum note computes the same graph and its eigenvalues, but not its independence number or any 18/19 extremal certificate. Our exact 19-clique cover and eight-block finite obstruction solve a natural extremal problem not implied by the published rank, valency or spectrum alone. An earlier unpublished exact graph optimization remains possible.
residual_risks: The independence number could have been calculated earlier without a findable public statement, including as an unpublished extension to the exact 85-line incidence graph.
The 85-line completeness theorem is accepted from the motivating peer-accessible preprint, not independently proved here.
The original Miyaoka article was not read; its quoted bound is obtained from the inspected primary 2026 source.

value.rationale: The largest set of pairwise disjoint lines is a natural and explicitly motivated geometrical capacity for the 85-line record quintic. The exact sharp value 18 distinguishes it from different 79-line examples having 24 skew lines in the same primary paper. The result is neither the trivial existence of a small skew subset nor a restatement of known graph spectrum: the upper bound uses a nontrivial finite 19-clique-cover obstruction and exact exhaustive residual transversal proof. This numerical invariant is a useful precise datum in comparing configurations and effective divisor geometry.
